summary: Topiramate is a broad-spectrum antiepileptic drug used as monotherapy and adjunctive therapy for partial-onset and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and for the preventive treatment of migraine. It acts through several mechanisms including sodium-channel blockade, GABA-A potentiation, AMPA/kainate glutamate antagonism, and carbonic anhydrase inhibition. The carbonic anhydrase effect underlies metabolic acidosis and kidney stone risk. Key risks include acute myopia with secondary angle-closure glaucoma, oligohidrosis with hyperthermia (especially in children), cognitive/neuropsychiatric effects, the antiepileptic-class suicidal behavior warning, and teratogenicity (oral clefts and small-for-gestational-age infants). Withdraw gradually to avoid increased seizure frequency.
indications: Initial monotherapy for partial-onset or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients 2 years and older
Adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures, primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, or seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in patients 2 years and older
Preventive treatment of migraine in patients 12 years and older

moa: The precise antiseizure and migraine-prevention mechanisms are unknown, but preclinical studies show four relevant properties at pharmacologically relevant concentrations: blockade of voltage-dependent sodium channels, augmentation of GABA activity at some GABA-A receptor subtypes, antagonism of the AMPA/kainate subtype of the glutamate receptor, and inhibition of carbonic anhydrase (especially isozymes II and IV).

absolute: History of hypersensitivity reaction to topiramate or any inactive ingredient (anaphylaxis and angioedema have occurred)
relative: Concomitant other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors or ketogenic diet (acidosis/stone risk)
monitor: Concomitant lithium at high topiramate doses
Children on prolonged therapy (growth, bone mineral density)

preg: Topiramate can cause fetal harm. Pregnancy registry data show an increased risk of major congenital malformations, including cleft lip and/or cleft palate, and of being small for gestational age (SGA); SGA appears dose-dependent and is more frequent with higher doses and use later in pregnancy. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; counsel patients of reproductive potential and encourage enrollment in the North American Antiepileptic Drug Pregnancy Registry (1-888-233-2334).
lact: Topiramate is excreted in human milk; effects on milk production are unknown. Diarrhea and somnolence have been reported in breastfed infants of mothers taking topiramate. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: In renal impairment (CrCl <70 mL/min/1.73m2) use one-half the usual adult dose. Clearance falls about 42% in moderate and 54% in severe renal impairment. Topiramate is cleared by hemodialysis (dialysis clearance ~120 mL/min vs 20-30 mL/min oral clearance), so a supplemental dose may be required to avoid rapid drops in plasma concentration.
hepatic: Plasma clearance of topiramate decreases by a mean of about 26% in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment; use with caution.

major: Other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (zonisamide, acetazolamide) - increased metabolic acidosis and kidney stone risk
Valproic acid - hypothermia and hyperammonemia with/without encephalopathy
CNS depressants and alcohol - additive CNS depression; use with extreme caution
Estrogen/progestin contraceptives - decreased efficacy and breakthrough bleeding, especially at doses >200 mg/day
moderate: Phenytoin or carbamazepine - clinically significant decrease in topiramate levels (may need dose adjustment)
Lithium - monitor lithium levels with high-dose topiramate
Hydrochlorothiazide - increases topiramate Cmax/AUC; may need topiramate dose decrease
minor: Pioglitazone - changes in exposure of unknown clinical significance
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; bioavailability is not affected by food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; topiramate can cause CNS depression and the combination has not been studied.
interactions.diagnostics: Can lower serum bicarbonate (hyperchloremic, non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis) and raise blood ammonia.

common: Cognitive slowing / difficulty with concentration and memory
serious: Acute myopia with secondary angle-closure glaucoma
Decreased bone mineral density and impaired growth in children
emergency: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)/multiorgan hypersensitivity
Acute secondary angle-closure glaucoma with visual loss

monitoring: Serum bicarbonate at baseline and periodically (metabolic acidosis)
Mood and behavior for emergence of depression or suicidal ideation
Visual symptoms; evaluate promptly for acute myopia/angle-closure glaucoma
Decreased sweating and elevated body temperature, particularly in children
Blood ammonia if encephalopathic symptoms or unexplained lethargy/vomiting occur
Growth (height/weight) and bone mineral density in children on prolonged therapy
counsel: Swallow tablets whole; do not break them (bitter taste)
Drink plenty of fluids to lower the chance of kidney stones
Report any vision changes, eye pain, or redness immediately
Watch for and report new or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm
In hot weather watch for decreased sweating and overheating, especially in children
Use effective contraception and tell your provider if pregnant or planning pregnancy; topiramate can harm the fetus
Do not stop suddenly - the dose must be tapered
pk: Rapid absorption; steady-state in ~4 days with normal renal function
Approximately 2 hours after a 400 mg oral dose
Dosed twice daily; ~70% eliminated unchanged in urine
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture; dispense in tight container
pearls: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition drives both metabolic acidosis and kidney stones - check bicarbonate and keep patients hydrated
Acute myopia/secondary angle-closure glaucoma typically occurs within the first month; discontinue topiramate as soon as possible
Oligohidrosis with hyperthermia is most common in children - counsel about heat exposure
Doses above 400 mg/day give no added benefit in adult partial-onset seizures
Carbamazepine and phenytoin lower topiramate levels; valproate combination risks hyperammonemia and hypothermia
Contraceptive efficacy can fall (even without breakthrough bleeding) at doses >200 mg/day
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, but skip it if it is almost time for the next dose; do not take a double dose. Do not stop topiramate abruptly - sudden discontinuation can increase seizure frequency, so any discontinuation should be done gradually under medical supervision.
overdose: Overdose signs and symptoms include convulsions, drowsiness, speech disturbance, blurred vision, diplopia, impaired mentation, lethargy, abnormal coordination, stupor, hypotension, abdominal pain, agitation, dizziness, and depression; severe metabolic acidosis can occur and deaths have been reported. Discontinue topiramate and give general supportive care; hemodialysis is an effective means of removing topiramate from the body.
